note: Every phrase a derivation.reads list may use, which check reads it, and which observable archive operation it corresponds to. Round 4's review found that derivation.reads was bound by nothing: `every class file, fully disassembled` could be written into two records and the gate still exited 0. Round 4's answer was this file, and round 5's review found what that answer is worth on its own: every link in it is a filename. It injected a reader of 1,113 class-file bodies into checks/surfaces-model.sh, changed no entry here and no record, and the gate exited 0 with every record still claiming metadata-only. A phrase is a claim about code, and a table of phrases cannot check code. So the phrases are no longer the ground: checks/verify-reads.sh runs each producer with Python's zipfile and the unzip binary wrapped, classifies every listing and every byte that came back, refuses any read of an entry body outright, and requires the set of operations a producer was seen performing to equal the set the observedAs fields below claim for it. This file is now the vocabulary and the claim; the run is the evidence. The producers map still decides which phrases a record may carry, so a record that omits an input its own model reads still fails in verify-provenance.sh, which is round 4's NB2.
